title: Know where you stand: net worth, cash flow and five health numbers

say: Know where you stand: net worth, cash flow, and five health numbers.
This is the video for Module 1 of Financial Literacy and Personal Finance Management.
Two women can each earn about 150,000 naira a month. One owns land and savings and owes nothing. The other owes a loan app and a cooperative. Same income, very different position.

say: An asset is anything you own that has money value. Value it at what you could realistically sell it for this month, not what you paid. A freezer bought for 250,000 naira may only sell for about 120,000 today.

cards.d: Anything you own with money value: cash, bank and wallet balances, cooperative savings, stock, land.
Any money you owe: a bank loan, a loan app balance, money from a relative, supplier credit, rent arrears.
Total assets minus total liabilities. It can be negative. It is a number to work on, not a judgement.

say: A liability is any money you owe, including money borrowed from family and stock taken on credit.

cards.d: Anything you own with money value: cash, bank and wallet balances, cooperative savings, stock, land.
Any money you owe: a bank loan, a loan app balance, money from a relative, supplier credit, rent arrears.
Total assets minus total liabilities. It can be negative. It is a number to work on, not a judgement.

say: Net worth is what you own minus what you owe. A negative number is not a judgement. It is a clear number you can work on.

cards.d: Anything you own with money value: cash, bank and wallet balances, cooperative savings, stock, land.
Any money you owe: a bank loan, a loan app balance, money from a relative, supplier credit, rent arrears.
Total assets minus total liabilities. It can be negative. It is a number to work on, not a judgement.

say: Ngozi sits down with a notebook.
She owns cash, a bank account, an Opay wallet, cooperative savings, shop stock and a deep freezer. Together, 569,500 naira.
She owes a cooperative loan, 50,000 naira to her sister, and supplier credit for rice. Together, 305,000 naira.
569,500 minus 305,000 gives a net worth of 264,500 naira.
Most of her assets are stock and cooperative savings she cannot turn into cash quickly, so she needs more easy-to-reach savings. She will redo this sheet every three months and watch the trend.
Step one. Open last month's statements in your bank and wallet apps, and add cash spending from your notebook.

say: Step three. Group everything. Occasional costs are the line people forget. School fees of about 180,000 naira a term are 540,000 a year, or 45,000 naira a month. Show that 45,000 every month and fees stop being a shock.

say: Step four. Money in minus all costs is your surplus or deficit. If there was a deficit, note how it was covered. A loan app is more urgent than a dip into savings.

say: Aisha builds her February statement from her bank app, her Moniepoint wallet and her notebook.
Her salary and perfume profit bring in 227,000 naira.
Fixed costs, including rent, data and a loan repayment, are 71,000 naira.
Variable costs like food and transport are 117,000 naira. Food is the biggest.
Her monthly share of school fees and gas is 24,000 naira.
That leaves a surplus of 15,000 naira. Adding the 25,000 she repaid on her loan, her savings rate is about 17.6%.
If your income changes a lot, plan fixed costs around your lowest month, not the average.
Five numbers tell you what needs attention first. Is your savings rate positive?

panel.heading: Five numbers, every quarter
items: Savings rate: is it positive?
Emergency cover: months of essential costs
Debt repayments as a share of income
Debt to assets: owe less than you own?
Net worth trend: is it rising?

say: Emergency cover is easy-to-reach savings divided by essential monthly costs. For example, Halima, a teacher in Abuja, had 45,000 naira against costs of 150,000. That is about nine days.

say: These numbers are private. Keep your sheet in a safe notebook or a locked note, and download statements yourself.

panel.heading: Protect your numbers
left: Use a locked note on your phone

say: Bank statements show your account number and balances. Never send them to strangers, or to anyone who contacts you claiming to help with a loan.

panel.heading: Protect your numbers
left: Use a locked note on your phone

say: To remember. Net worth is what you own minus what you owe. Value things at today's resale price. Show occasional costs every month. Watch your savings rate. And fix one weak number at a time.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Net worth = what you own minus what you owe
Value assets at today's resale price
Show occasional costs as a monthly share
Savings rate = money kept / money in
Fix the first weak number only
